subject: Business
title: Spanish Silver and the Price Revolution
description: A 60-second lesson on Spanish Silver and the Price Revolution.

hook.text: Spain flooded Europe with silver from the Americas. Prices tripled in a century. Nobody understood why.

buildup.text: Between 1500 and 1650, massive silver imports from Potosí and Mexico transformed European economies.

discovery.text: More money chasing the same goods means higher prices. This was one of history's first inflations.

twist.text: Paradoxically, Spain — the richest country — went bankrupt six times. Easy money funded wars, not productivity.

climax.text: The Dutch and English, with less silver but better institutions, overtook Spain economically.

punchline.text: More money doesn't mean more wealth. It just means higher prices.

quiz.question: Why did Spain go bankrupt despite having the most silver?
options: The silver funded wars instead of productive investment

details.summary: Spain's massive importation of silver from New World mines in the 16th century caused the Price Revolution, a sustained period of inflation across Europe as the money supply expanded dramatically. Prices roughly quadrupled over 150 years, transforming European economies.
details.whyItMatters: The Price Revolution is the earliest large-scale demonstration that increasing money supply causes inflation. This historical episode established the quantity theory of money that remains central to monetary economics today.
takeaways: Spanish silver from the Americas quadrupled European money supply over 150 years
Prices across Europe roughly quadrupled during the 16th century Price Revolution
The episode established the link between money supply growth and inflation

faq.question: Where did all the Spanish silver come from?
faq.answer: Primarily from the Potosi mine in Bolivia and Mexican silver mines. Spain extracted enormous quantities through forced indigenous labor. Silver was shipped across the Atlantic in treasure fleets, flooding European markets with unprecedented amounts of precious metal money.

faq.question: How did the Price Revolution transform European society?
faq.answer: Rising prices bankrupted the Spanish crown despite its silver wealth. Fixed-income aristocrats lost purchasing power while merchants and artisans who could raise prices prospered. The economic upheaval contributed to the rise of capitalism and the decline of feudalism.
